subtopics.title: Store-and-Forward Packet Switching
subtopics.summary: How packet switches receive, store, and retransmit packets; per-hop transmission delay and computing the end-to-end delay of a message crossing N links and N-1 switches.

subtopics.title: Queuing Delay, Packet Loss, and Statistical Multiplexing
subtopics.summary: Output buffers in packet switches, queuing delay when packets arrive faster than the output link can transmit, packet loss under congestion, and how statistical multiplexing shares link capacity on demand.

subtopics.title: Circuit Switching with FDM and TDM
subtopics.summary: Dedicated end-to-end circuits with reserved bandwidth, circuit setup and teardown, and how frequency-division and time-division multiplexing partition a link among active circuits.

subtopics.title: Packet Switching vs. Circuit Switching
subtopics.summary: Trade-offs between the two core approaches: efficiency for bursty traffic, wasted capacity during silent periods, guaranteed versus on-demand bandwidth, and why the Internet adopts packet switching.

subtopics.title: The Internet as a Network of Networks
subtopics.summary: How access ISPs (home, mobile, enterprise) interconnect through regional ISPs, national and global tier-1 providers, peering, IXPs, and content provider networks to form today's Internet structure.
